newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Filipino ghosts come marching in on All Saints Day.
newsitem.headline: Filipino ghosts come marching in on All Saints Day.

text.p: Thousands of Filipinos visited cemeteries on Friday to spend the weekend with their beloved dead, an annual ritual which Manila newspapers highlighted with tales of ghosts at the presidential palace.
Roads leading to the city's graveyards were choked with cars and jeepney mini-buses as entire families carrying picnic hampers of beer, food and music players headed for the tombs.

All Saints Day on November 1 and All Souls Day the following day is a time for merry-making as much as memories, when an overnight stay in tents by the tombs ensures the graves are clean and the departed remembered.

But the newspapers and others used the occasion to call attention to government inaction over responsibility for a deadly disco fire and to the unknown fate of political dissidents, saying these ghosts cried out for justice.
The Philippine Daily Inquirer newspaper ran a front page story with hazy pictures of what it said were ghosts in a burnt-out wreck that was once the Ozone Disco.
The disco caught fire in March last year, and more than 150 people, mostly teenagers celebrating the end of the school year, died.
The Inquirer said the teenagers' ghosts were crying out for justice as city officials responsible for granting a permit to the building had yet to be charged.
The government said the fire was caused by a short circuit in overloaded electric cables and that the people were trapped inside because there were not enough exits.
The pictures published by the Inquirer were taken by the victims' relatives last month to present as evidence in court.
"Of these photos, about a dozen showed these mysterious entities captured in film," the paper said.

"White, floating head and body outlined against the wall," said the caption to one hazy picture while another said: "Two faces peering out of a wooden beam." The images were far from clear to dispassionate observers.
The Manila Times marked All Saints Day with a report about ghosts knocking at the doors of Malacanang presidential palace.
"In Malacanang, the ghosts groan and sigh. They knock on doors and leap over shoulders or call reporters by their names. The ghosts at the palace do all this in daylight," it said.

Human rights group Amnesty International marked the day of the dead with a reminder of more than 1,600 people who were "disappeared". It said these people "disappeared at the hands of the state and are presumed to lie in hidden graves".
The late Ferdinand Marcos, who ruled the Philippines with an iron hand until his overthrow in a popular revolt in 1986, stands accused of widespread human rights violations.
Amnesty said it would release a detailed report on the disappearances and hold a rally at a Manila church on Saturday.
